{{Short description|Russian physicist}}
'''Yury (or Yuriy or Yuri) Mikhailovich Bunkov (Юрий Михайлович Буньков, 29 August 1950 – 4 October 2026) (source) was a Russian experimental physicist specializing in condensed matter physics.'''<ref name=AcademiaEuropaea>{{citation|title=Yury Bunkov|website=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Bunkov_Yury}}</ref> He was known as one of the co-discoverers of the [[Quantum spin liquid|quantum spin liquid state]].<ref name=FritzLondonPrize>{{cite web|title=The 2008 Fritz London Memorial Prize Winners|website=physics.duke.edu|url=https://physics.duke.edu/sites/physics.duke.edu/files/documents/BunkovDmitrievFomin2008.pdf}}</ref> https://kpfu.ru/physics/kollektiv-instituta-fiziki-s-priskorbiem-493243.html

==Education and career==
Bunkov, born into a family of geologists, graduated in 1968 from a special school for physics and mathematics in Moscow (School No. 2). In 1968 he also achieved first place in the [[Soviet Student Olympiads|Moscow Physics Olympiad]] and matriculated at the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] (MIPT), which was headed by [[Piotr Kapitza]].<ref name=RoyalSociety>{{cite web|title=Cosmology meets condensed matter (Event type: discussion meetings)|date=January 2008|website=The Royal Society)|url=http://royalsociety.org/Cosmology-meets-condensed-matter/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011223504/http://royalsociety.org/Cosmology-meets-condensed-matter/|archive-date=2011-10-11}}</ref>

According to Bunkov,<ref name=RoyalSociety/> the "parametric echo"<ref>{{cite journal|author=Petrov, M. P.|author2=Ivanov, A. V.|author3=Korneev, V. R.|author4=Andreeva, G. T.|year=1980|title=Parametric echo and magnetoelastic excitation of NMR in FeBO<sub>3</sub>|journal=Soviet Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics|volume=51|pages=578|bibcode=1980JETP...51..578P|url=http://www.jetp.ras.ru/cgi-bin/dn/e_051_03_0578.pdf}}</ref> should be called the "Bunkov echo":
{{blockquote|As a student I observed and explained the "parametric echo", now named the Bunkov echo.  That is the echo signal seen in magnetically ordered materials after a single resonance and a single parametric pulse.}}

In 1974 he matriculated at the [[Institute for Physical Problems|Kapitza Institute for Physical Problems]], where he received in 1979 his [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree (Ph.D.).<ref name=RoyalSociety/> A. S. Borovik-Romanov<ref>{{cite journal|date=January 1998|volume=51|issue=1|page=75|doi=10.1063/1.882134|title=Obituary. Andrey Stanislavovich Borovik-Romanov|author=Andreev, Alexander F.|author-link=Alexander F. Andreev|author2=Dmitriev,, Vladmir V.|journal=Physics Today|bibcode=1998PhT....51a..75A|doi-access=free}}</ref> was Bunkov's thesis advisor.<ref name=RoyalSociety/> At the Kapitza Institute for Physical Problems, he was employed as a non-principal scientist from 1979 to 1985, a principal scientist from 1985 to 1986, and from 1986 to 1995 as a leading scientist.<ref name=AcademiaEuropaea/> At the Kapitza Institute he constructed the Soviet Union's first nuclear demagnetization refrigerator.<ref name=FritzLondonPrize/>

In 1983 at the Kapitza Institute, quantum spin [[superfluidity]] was discovered by Bunkov, who was the team leader, with Vladimir Dmitriev and Yuri Mukharsky (who worked at the Kapitza Institute as students). Spin superfluidity manifested itself in [[NMR]] studies on [[Helium-3|<sup>3</sup>helium]]-B as regions of coherent [[Larmor precession]] (regions known as HPDs, Homogeneously Precessing Domains), with inhomogeneities in the precession caused by supercurrents in the spin (based on magnetization) similar to those in superconductivity (based on charge-supercurrent) and superliquid or [[Bose-Einstein condensate]]s (based on mass-supercurrent). Spin superfluidity is also a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) of [[magnon]]s. A theoretical explanation was given in the 1980s by the theorist Igor Akindinovich Fomin.

Bunkov wrote concerning his work at the Kapitza Institute:<ref name=RoyalSociety/>
{{blockquote|In 1982 our group succeeded in cooling [[Helium-3|<sup>3</sup>He]] into the superfluid state and in the following year we discovered spin superfluidity, the superflow of <sup>3</sup>He magnetization with no mass current. We observed the formation of a magnetically coherent state which is now considered a [[Bose-Einstein condensation]] of [[magnon]]s. We also observed the magnetic Josephson effect, critical spin supercurrent, phase slippage and other spin coherent phenomena.}}

{{blockquote|... The first magnonic superfluid state was discovered in 1984 by A. S. Borovik-Romanov and Yu. M. Bunkov experimental group and described theoretically by I. Fomin as a new state of magnetically ordered matter ... It was observed as the spontaneously self-organized phase-coherent precession of spins in an antiferromagnetic superfluid <sup>3</sup>He-B. This state fulfills all criteria of coherence, suggested later by [[David Snoke|Snoke]] ... It is radically different from the conventional ordered states in magnets. It is the quasi-equilibrium one, which emerges on the background of the ordered magnetic state, and which can be described in terms of the condensation of magnetic excitations to a coherent quantum state ...<ref>{{cite journal|author=Bunkov, Yury|title=Spin superfluid state at room temperature|journal=AIP Conference Proceedings|series=Fifth International Conference on Quantum Technologies (Icqt-2019)|volume=2241|issue=1|page=020006|publisher=AIP Publishing LLC|year=2020|doi=10.1063/5.0011601|bibcode=2020AIPC.2241b0006B|s2cid=226435978|doi-access=free}} (This article contains a discussion of HPDs.)</ref>}}

At the Kapitza Institute, he received in 1985 his Russian [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree ([[habilitation]])<ref name=RoyalSociety/> with a thesis on NMR studies on superfluid helium-3. At Grenoble's ''[[Institut Néel]]'' (formerly called CRTBT), belonging to the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|''Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique'' (CNRS)]], he was employed from 1995 to 2004 as a ''Directeur de Recherche'' and since 2004 is employed as a ''Directeur de Recherche de 1<sup>er</sup> classe''. From 2008 to the present, he is a part-time professor at [[Kazan Federal University]].<ref name=AcademiaEuropaea/>

For many years Bunkov participated in the Soviet-Finnish project ROTA, in which the researchers discovered many different types of <sup>3</sup>He vortices.<ref name=RoyalSociety/> He also made many visits (from 1989 to 1995) to [[Lancaster University]], where he participated in NMR experiments at record-setting low temperatures for <sup>3</sup>He.<ref name=RoyalSociety/>

At CRTBT his research group cooled <sup>3</sup>He to 100 [[Kelvin|K]] and, at such low temperatures, found in 1996 an energy deficit after a <sup>3</sup>He neutron capture reaction. The energy deficit "appeared to arise from vortex creation via the Kibble-Zurek cosmological mechanism, in analogy with cosmic-string creation in the early Universe."<ref name=RoyalSociety/> He became the leader of the project ULTIMA (Ultra Low Temperature Instrumentation for Measurements in Astrophysics), which has as its purpose the development of a dark-matter detector based on overcooled superfluid <sup>3</sup>He.<ref name=RoyalSociety/><ref>{{cite journal|author=Bunkov, Y.|author2=Godfrin, H.|author3=Winkelmann, C.|year=1996|title=ULTIMA|journal=Nature|volume=382|page=332|url=https://www.hep.shef.ac.uk/conferences/idm2004/talks/tuesday/pdfs/bunkov_yuriy.pdf}}</ref>

In the <sup>3</sup>He-B phase (which has a complex phase structure)<ref>Since <sup>3</sup>He has spin 1/2 and is a fermion, the superconductivity in the <sup>3</sup>He-B phase corresponds to the [[Cooper pair]] formation into composite bosons as in a superconductor in which p-wave Cooper pairs occur.</ref> he experimentally discovered analogues to cosmological and quantum field theoretical phenomena, such as cosmological strings (as vortices in the spin supercurrent) and Majorana quasiparticles. In the 1980s he and his colleagues detected Goldstone modes (as phonons in the spin-superfluidity HPDs analogous to the [[second sound]] phenomena in superfluids). In the 2000s he discovered [[Q-ball]]s] in superfluid <sup>3</sup>He. (The concept of a Q-ball, a type of non-topological [[soliton]], was originally introduced in quantum field theory.)

He collaborated extensively with the theorist [[Grigori Efimovich Volovik]]. In 2008, Bunkov and his Japanese colleagues discovered coherent precession in the helium-3-A phase embedded in uniaxially deformed [[Anisotropy|anisotropic]] [[aerogel]]s.

Bunkov is internationally recognized for his research on quantum fluids and solids, superfluid <sup>3</sup>He nuclear magnetic resonance {NMR), and oltra-low temperatures techniques and their application to cosmology and the search for [[dark matter]].<ref name=AcademiaEuropaea/> As of the end of 2018 his [[Hirsch index]] was 26.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bunkov Yurii Mikhailovich|website=Kazan Federal University|url=https://kpfu.ru/pec_print?p_id=24760&p_lang=2}}</ref>

Bunkov received in 1993 the [[State Prize of the Russian Federation]] "for the discovery of magnetic superfluidity and the Homogeneously Precessing Domain".<ref name=AcademiaEuropaea/> In 2001 Bunkov was made Doctor "Honoris Causa" by [[Pavol Jozef Šafárik University]] in [[Košice]], Slovakia.<ref name=AcademiaEuropaea/> In 2008 he was awarded, jointly  with Vladimir Dmitriev and Igor A. Fomin, the [[Fritz London Memorial Prize]] for their discovery and elucidation of "unique phenomena in superfluid <sup>3</sup>He-B: macroscopi phase-coherent spin precession and the flow of spin supercurrent."<ref name=FritzLondonPrize/> Bunkov has been a full member of the [[Academia Europaea]] since 2010.<ref name=AcademiaEuropaea/>
